\title{VOSS: Serverless Functions on Attested Volunteer Machines}

\author{Aalhad Sawane}
\affiliation{\institution{\todo{institution}}\country{\todo{country}}}
\email{aalhadsawane@gmail.com}

\begin{abstract}
We study serverless functions whose results are due within seconds, served by home and office machines that their
owners lend. An owner can take a machine back at any moment and cannot be trusted with the code and data it runs.
Each machine therefore boots a measured image and proves it by remote attestation before it receives the key that
decrypts a function; an owner who does not physically attack the machine can then only switch it off or drop its
messages. \voss{} is an architecture and a scheduler for this setting. The scheduler chooses, within a limit the tenant
sets on how many machines may hold a function's key, the key holders and warm sandboxes that serve the most
invocations on time when machines differ in speed per function and leave without notice; it places each invocation
by its probability of meeting its deadline; and it runs an invocation on a second machine when the first does not
answer in time.
\critical{Headline result (held-out experiments): deadlines met at a stated holder limit, VOSS against the best of
the keep-alive, histogram and autoscaling policies; failure result if supported.}
\critical{Basis sentence: simulator driven by public traces, calibrated on N machines, checked against an N-worker
emulation; N after calibration and validation.}
\end{abstract}
